name: cAMP-PKA Pathway (Glucose Sensing)
description: The cAMP-dependent protein kinase A (PKA) pathway in S. cerevisiae senses glucose availability and activates growth programs. Glucose binding to the GPCR Gpr1 activates the G-protein Gpa2, which stimulates adenylate cyclase Cyr1 to produce cAMP. cAMP binds to the regulatory subunit Bcy1, releasing the catalytic subunits Tpk1/2/3 which phosphorylate targets to promote glycolysis, ribosome biogenesis, and growth while repressing stress responses and gluconeogenesis. The pathway integrates with Ras (Ras1/2-GTP also activates Cyr1) and cross-talks with TOR. Under glucose starvation, low cAMP causes Bcy1 to inhibit PKA, activating Msn2/4 stress transcription factors and enabling Snf1 (AMPK) to activate alternative carbon utilization. The pathway controls the growth-quiescence decision based on glucose availability.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on extensive research on yeast PKA pathway components (Gpr1, Gpa2, Cyr1, Bcy1, Tpk1/2/3) and regulation. The pathway is highly conserved and serves as a model for mammalian GPCR-cAMP signaling. All components and mechanisms are well-validated.

notes: PKA pathway demonstrates GPCR signaling in yeast. High AND gate count for signal integration (Gpa2 + Ras converge on Cyr1). Cross-talk with TOR and Snf1 creates nutrient sensing network.
